newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end week at another record close.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end week at another record close.

text.p: Swiss shares kept up this week's record-setting pace, posting a fourth consecutive record close on Friday on the back of a soaring dollar, derivatives-linked buying, and a host of rumours in the financial sector.
"Today's extreme moves seemed exaggerated," one trader said, citing a late jump by most-active UBS bearers of 60 francs, or 3.73 percent, to 1,670.
CS Group, which has been at the centre of spin-off and alliance speculation lately, shook off early weakness to surge 2.25 francs to 196.50.
The blue-chip SMI ended up 68.8 points, or 1.31 percent, at 5,320.0, narrowly off the all-time high of 5,327.6.
The all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) added 40.54 points, or 1.22 percent, to 3,368.53.
Bourse volume was rather high at 2.78 billion francs.
"It's not sure whether we will see a correction after this bull run," one dealer noted. "The market seems to know only one direction, namely up," he said.
The market shrugged off strong U.S. jobs data.
Another trader warned that if speculation in the financials sector should prove unfounded, the market may see a slump in the next few sessions.
Insurer Zurich was one of the biggest winners. Its stock climbed 22 francs, or more than four percent, to 556. The shares profited from an upgrade of CSFB's price target to 650 francs from 550.
Dollar-sensitive stocks such as Roche, ABB, Alusuisse, Holderbank, Ciba, Ares Serono were bolstered by the dollar's recent strength.
Novartis underperformed the market, adding five francs to 1,990.
Interroll ended the second day of trading 1.25 francs higher at 247.75.
